title: Fourth moment bound for a sliced function
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $d,e:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ and $f:\{-1,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$. Suppose that for every sign $b\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$; also suppose that $\mathbb E[d^4]\le 9(\mathbb E[d^2])^2$ and $\mathbb E[e^4]\le 81(\mathbb E[e^2])^2$, with expectations uniform on the respective cubes. Then $\mathbb E[f^4]\le 81(\mathbb E[f^2])^2$, with expectation uniform on the $(n+1)$-dimensional cube.
hypotheses_covered: $d$ and $e$ are real-valued functions on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional sign cube
For every first-coordinate sign and remaining input, $f(b,x)=bd(x)+e(x)$
